description: Challenge C1 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Myriad begins with /mɪr/ in General American. Married begins with /mær/, merriment with /mɛ/, and moraine with /mə/.
Quintessential begins with /kwɪn/. Questionable begins with /kwɛs/, quarantine with /kwɔr/ or /kwɑr/, and quiescent with /kwaɪ/.
Vigilant begins with /vɪ/. Valiant begins with /væ/, vagrant with /veɪ/, and voluble with /vɑ/.
Psoriasis begins with /s/ because the initial p is silent. Zoology begins with /z/, theory with /θ/, and fiscal with /f/.
Pteranodon begins with /t/ because its initial p is silent. Pivotal begins with /p/, theory with /θ/, and gnawing with /n/.
Chthonic begins with /θ/; the initial ch is silent and the th supplies the first sound. Kinetic begins with /k/, shallow with /ʃ/, and gnawing with /n/.
Asks ends with /sks/. Ask ends with /sk/, asked with /skt/, and asking with /skɪŋ/.
Twelfths ends with /lfθs/, adding /s/ to the final cluster in twelfth. Twelve ends with /lv/, and twelfthly adds a syllable.
Crisps ends with /s/ after /sp/, producing /sps/. Crisp lacks the final /s/, crisis ends with /sɪs/, and crisped ends with /pt/.
Hors d'oeuvre is pronounced /ɔr ˈdɜrv/ in General American; its written French sequence is highly irregular. The other choices have different syllable and consonant patterns.
Onomatopoeia is pronounced /ˌɑnəˌmætəˈpiːə/. Onomatopoeic has a related but different ending; onomastic and onomatology have different stress and vowel sequences.
Ecclesiastical is pronounced /ɪˌkliːziˈæstɪkəl/. The alternatives differ in their stressed syllables and vowel-consonant sequences.
